correctness.rationale: The five independent twin classes form a complete-adjacency blow-up of the cyclic class graph in the stated order. Each nonsaturated class needs a selected neighbor class; each legal defense removes a selected vertex from an adjacent class and must restore that condition in all nonsaturated classes. These are exact tests because vertex choices within each class are interchangeable. For every profile of total at most five, including after a swap, saturation of a nonsingleton class of capacity at least five is possible only with five vertices all in that class. Such a profile fails domination because a class at distance two has no selected neighbor, so replacing the four capacities by six preserves domination and security on all profiles in question. Independently checked one explicit representative per occupancy using bitset domination and individual swaps: for sizes 0 through 5 the candidate/dominating/secure triples are (1,0,0), (5,0,0), (14,0,0), (30,6,0), (55,19,0), (91,41,6); the six profiles match exactly. The product of the five binomial factors counts each labelled profile without overlap. An additional exact check of all actual labelled subsets of sizes 0 through 5 at (5,5), (5,6), (6,6) confirmed the entire profile histograms and totals 2225, 3435, 5301. The all-parameter result relies on the capacity argument and exhaustive fixed profile census, not on the sample graphs.
